A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Video2BEV work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary sections are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval experiments on UniV, component and training ablations in Tables 2–3, and qualitative analyses in the supplement.

after.justification: v2 retains the original UniV experiments and adds SUES-200 evaluation in Table 2b and a loss-weight experiment in Table 4.

M1.justification: Both versions use SfM/3DGS BEV reconstruction, diffusion-generated hard negatives, and the same two-stage retrieval and reranking pipeline. Expanded explanations and the new loss-weight ablation do not establish a revision to the default method.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation on real-world SUES-200, extending coverage beyond the simulated UniV data. Both versions retain UniV's 30° and 45° subsets and bidirectional drone–satellite retrieval tasks.

E2.justification: LPN, FSRA, DWDR, and Sample4Geo remain the evaluated comparators on UniV. The same set is used for the new SUES-200 comparison. GeNIe is newly discussed but is not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a cross-dataset evaluation design: a model trained on UniV at 45° is tested on unseen SUES-200 at 45° without fine-tuning. Appendix Section 10 also adds a controlled first-stage loss-weight sweep over 0.1, 0.5, and 1. The existing UniV evaluation design is otherwise retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds synthetic-to-real distribution-shift testing, SUES-200 failure cases in Figure 12b, and sensitivity analysis of the contrastive-loss weight in Table 4. These extend the questions tested beyond v1's retained component, training-strategy, top-k, and occlusion analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The additional experiments retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Table 2b adds SUES-200 results: Video2BEV obtains 91.50 AP for drone-to-satellite and 92.53 AP for satellite-to-drone, versus Sample4Geo's 84.14 and 88.80. Table 4 adds first-stage loss-weight results, and Figures 7 and 12 add SUES retrieval examples. The retained UniV Tables 2/2a and 3 have unchanged scores.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(4) retain the same loss and similarity definitions. The new appendix explicitly combines the existing first-stage losses using a weight for empirical sensitivity testing; it introduces no substantive theoretical reasoning, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The Video2BEV and UniV contributions remain intact. The introduction and conclusion add a claim of generalization to unseen real-world SUES-200 without fine-tuning, extending the earlier claims supported only by UniV experiments.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the SUES-200 results as evidence of OOD generalization and adds an applicability assumption that a known search area permits offline BEV preprocessing. It also explains diffusion-noise variation while retaining captions. Existing occlusion and appearance-mismatch limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds input resolution, GPU allocations, BEV rendering time, default loss weights, and a statement that data will be released upon acceptance. However, it omits v1's explicit 2-fps training/testing setting, 32 synthetic negatives per view/location, and human involvement in caption generation. These are documentation changes, without evidence that the underlying settings changed.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially revised around image-based and video-based geo-localization, adding discussion of prior video-localization approaches including GAMA and CityGuessr. New positioning relative to GaussianBEV and GeNIe further contextualizes reconstruction and hard-negative generation, beyond citation or bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The introduction is extensively rewritten around occlusion and viewpoint disparity, contributions are consolidated, and related work is reorganized. Method explanations and terminology are revised throughout, two supplementary sections are added, and the author block expands from two authors to four.

P2.justification: The visual format is retained with localized revisions: Figures 2 and 3 exchange positions, AP plots gain numerical labels, and Figure 4 clarifies weight sharing and losses. New result tables and SUES panels are added. Synthetic examples are exchanged between Figures 5 and 11 rather than newly added.

improvement.justification: v1 motivates real-world drone localization but validates retrieval only on simulated UniV data. v2 substantially addresses this gap through unseen real-world SUES-200 testing, comparative results, and failure examples. The loss-weight study and stronger research positioning provide further support. Removing explicit frame-rate and synthetic-sample counts weakens reproducibility, but the new external validation provides a substantial overall gain.
